44bcbb4f0bb6ca3ca6a74be91d08b24172bf76b0.summary: The report, published by The Hacker News on 2025-04-02, describes FIN7, a financially motivated Russian cybercrime group, as linked to Anubis, a Python-based backdoor that gives remote access to compromised Windows systems. PRODAFT, a Swiss security company, is quoted on the malware's ability to give attackers full control. Anubis is believed to be spread through malspam that entices victims to run a payload hosted on compromised SharePoint sites. 44528d153681a19a67e9f595deaeaf3dff38e485.summary: WithSecure Intelligence reports late-March 2023 intrusions against internet-facing Veeam Backup & Replication servers, overlapping with FIN7 tradecraft or a threat actor using it. Initial access is likely via CVE-2023-27532, a low-to-medium confidence assessment. The attackers used PowerShell loaders (POWERTRASH, POWERHOLD), the DICELOADER backdoor and DUBLOADER, which side-loads through a Notepad++ binary. They then moved laterally and likely deployed Cobalt Strike. The report judges the scope limited and the goal unclear.

subject.name: FIN7 tradecraft attacks against Veeam backup servers

hedges: Initial access and execution are likely via CVE-2023-27532, but this is a low-to-medium confidence assessment with no concrete indicators confirming it.
Attribution is broadened from FIN7 to FIN7 or a threat actor utilizing FIN7 tradecraft.
No strong evidence links the earlier suspicious activity of 24 March 2023 to the intrusions; its reason remains unknown.
The payload of the secondary script could not be fully retrieved; the report believes it was likely a Cobalt Strike beacon.
The goal of these attacks was unclear at the time of writing, as they were mitigated before fully materializing.
The report believes the scope of the attack is limited, given the probable rarity of exposed Veeam servers on port 9401.
